_comment: Maps examined directly through the scan for tribal annotation, recording what
is actually printed on the face. This file exists because the catalogue is
silent: across 663 records the Dublin Core names a tribe in three, and two of
those three are 1:50 000 sheets that happen to be named after the district
they cover. Whether a map annotates tribes can only be settled by looking.
Sampling rule, so that a 'no' means something: each map was read in at least
one window of the interior - the Tell, the steppe, or the south, never the
coast alone - at full scan resolution, plus its legend where it has one. The
windows are recorded. A map coded no_annotation_seen is a map whose recorded
windows carried none; on a large sheet that is weaker evidence than a yes,
and `windows_read` is there so the next person can see how weak.
annotation_forms vocabulary:
territory_label      a tribe's name in letterspaced capitals across the
country it holds, with no boundary drawn
marked_tribe         a territory label carrying an explicit marker, (Tribu),
(Tribu des), (Tribus), TERRITOIRE DES
tribal_ksour         'Kt des X' / 'Ksour des X' - the tribe named through
its fortified granaries, the southern form
douar_toponym        a settlement printed Dr / Douar + a lineage name
lineage_toponym      any place name carrying Ouled / Oulad / Beni / ben
smala                a settlement named as a tribe's smala
glossary             a legend panel translating the tribal and settlement
vocabulary the map uses
thematic_distribution  the map's subject is the distribution of a mode of
habitation or population, mapped as areas
caidat_label         the caidat - the administrative unit built on the
tribe - named across its territory
admin_limit          drawn limits of caidats, controles civils, annexes,
or the territoire militaire

btv1b53136235q.title: Carte de la Régence de Tunis / par E. Pellissier
btv1b53136235q.note: The densest tribal annotation in the collection, and the earliest that is systematic. Names run in letterspaced capitals across the steppe and the Dahar; no boundary is drawn anywhere on the sheet. Pellissier wrote the Description de la Régence de Tunis as a member of the Commission scientifique d'Algérie, and the map is its plate.

btv1b531797046.title: Carte de la régence de Tunis, dressée au Dépôt de la guerre / d'après Falbe et Pricot de Sainte-Marie
btv1b531797046.note: Prints 'DOUARS OULED ARFA' as a label in its own right - the tribe located through its camps rather than by name alone - and scatters 'Douar' as a settlement class across the Tell.

btv1b53179703r.title: Carte de la Régence de Tunis dressée au Dépôt général de la guerre
btv1b53179703r.note: The earliest tribal annotation seen in this collection. Sparser than 1853 and concentrated on the Cap Bon in the window read.

btv1b84389986.title: Carte du théâtre de la guerre en Tunisie / dressée par Ch. Lasailly
btv1b84389986.tribes_seen: see config/tribal_labels_read.json - 69 labels transcribed with pixels
btv1b84389986.note: The exemplar, and the reason it is the one transcribed in full: it marks tribes explicitly with (Tribu) under the name, so the class is legible without inference. Published for the French public during the 1881 invasion, at 1:1 200 000 - a scale at which the tribe is one of the few things the sheet has room to say.

btv1b84446578.title: Carte du Voltaire. Expédition contre les Kroumirs
btv1b84446578.note: Carries 'Principaux noms indigènes employés dans cette carte' in three columns - noms arabes and noms kabyles with their meanings, Douar = cercle de tentes, Dechra = village, Bled = pays - so the sheet teaches its reader the vocabulary of the country it is invading. The only map in the collection to do so at this length.

btv1b53021186j.title: Carte de la Régence de Tunis (Garnier Frères)
btv1b53021186j.note: The same labels as the 1857 Dépôt de la guerre sheet, in the same places, down to 'DOUARS OULED ARFA'. A commercial reprint of military work; the annotation is inherited, not observed.

btv1b53024975r.title: Carte de la Tunisie, dressée au service géographique de l'armée
btv1b53024975r.note: The southern form: the tribe is named through its ksour, 'Kt des X', and the label sits on the granaries rather than on the grazing. Same tribes as the Taride thirty years later, named a different way.

btv1b530647344.title: Nouvelle carte de la Tunisie (Taride)
btv1b530647344.note: A commercial tourist map, and still carrying tribal country names in spaced type forty years into the protectorate. 'Smala des Souassi' near El Djem names a settlement for the tribe that founded it.

btv1b8442159r.title: Carte routière de la Tunisie / Touring Club de France
btv1b8442159r.note: Tribal names survive but are set so widely spaced that a letter can sit 8 km from its neighbour, and the green dashed administrative limits are printed more strongly than the names.

btv1b53179710t.title: Tunisie au 500.000e / Service géographique de l'armée
btv1b53179710t.note: The end state. The letterspaced capitals across the Tell are still there and still name a native unit, but the unit is now the caidat, and most caidats are named for their market town rather than for a tribe.

btv1b53213307c.title: Habitation rurale des indigènes (Atlas d'Algérie et de Tunisie)
btv1b53213307c.note: The only thematic ethnographic map in the collection. Six area classes - tentes, gourbis, maisons à terrasse, maisons à toit de tuiles, maisons à l'européenne, grottes et ghorfas - drawn as colour over Algeria and Tunisia, with the limits of the communes mixtes and contrôles civils. It maps how people live rather than which tribe they belong to, and the tent zone is the nomadic south; the ghorfa zone is the Matmata and Ouerghemma country.

btv1b8445503p.title: Environs de Medenine / Service géographique de l'Armée
tribes_seen: a letterspaced capital label cut by the window edge, reading ...A T
btv1b8445503p.note: Already coded tribes in config/inspected_sheets.json. The window read carries henchir and lineage names densely; the territory label itself was clipped.

btv1b53022873s.title: Carte des itinéraires de la Tunisie, 1:800 000
btv1b53022873s.note: No tribal annotation in the window read, which covers the central steppe - the country of the Hammama and the Frechiche on every other sheet of the period. What it carries instead is wells, and each well graded (E.B.) for water quality. An itinerary map answers a marching column's question, and the column's question was water.

btv1b8439078n.title: Etude sur la frontière de la Tunisie / par le général Lewal
btv1b8439078n.note: No tribal annotation in the window read. Place names are doubled with their Roman equivalents - Bulla Regia, Sicca Veneria, Musti, Narragara - which is the antiquarian register, not the ethnographic one.

oai:u-bordeaux-montaigne.fr:340491.title: Tunisie Flle. Pichon, 1:50 000
oai:u-bordeaux-montaigne.fr:340491.note: No tribe is named on the face. What the sheet carries is the grain below the tribe: Dr Zouamela and Dr el Abaida - the douar as a mapped settlement - and Hr Ouled el Hadj, Bir Ouled Ali. The letterspaced capitals that on a 1:800 000 sheet would be a tribe are here physical: KEF MAZIL, BLED EL..., GARAET EL ATEUCH.

oai:u-bordeaux-montaigne.fr:340528.title: Tunisie Flle. Chorbane, 1:50 000
oai:u-bordeaux-montaigne.fr:340528.note: Same pattern in Souassi and M'Talith country, where the 1881 and 1920 small-scale sheets both print a tribe: Dr en Nouilia, Dr Krelifa b. Slimane, Dr Belkassem b. Amor, Bir Oulad Achour, Bled el Azilik. The tribe is present as its lineages and absent as itself.
